title: Reduce QQ16 L2 native reconstruction from rank mass 1168 to 992
body:
PR2492 reconstructs QQ16's L2 ordinary record across the F0/B1 cut with native rank mass 1,168. This construction returns the **same F_L output frame** with rank mass **992**: 96 rank-one and 112 rank-eight children, all 200 source arrays restored, the same 96 owned outputs and 208 charged cover maps. Scalar allowance decreases from 6,624 to 6,610. At every rank-power price r^q, 0<q<=1, the local child saving is 304-16*8^q >=176.

The word copies Y into owned outputs before normalization and uses the packet's existing maps that preserve the entire accumulated frame. A separately stated variant keeps outputs in that accumulated frame for rank mass **224**; consuming those outputs downstream remains an open contract. Neither variant supplies a whole native decoder, favorable full supplier bill or new kappa.

Only `research/qq16-accumulated-frame-l2/` is added: the ordered arbitrary-array proof, both literal word variants, exact registered maps, source pins, complete invoices, verifier and failure controls. Canonical main base is `0fdd7d82de03e43c9e5a1000dfbcd380d1b687d2`, priority revision 4. The weighted picker selected recursive interfaces; TASK explicitly changes the full-controller card to PR2492's bounded frame/read obligation. The selected record and frozen predecessors are unchanged.

Validation on Windows x64 / **CPython 3.12.10**:

    python3.12 scripts/research_package.py --package research/qq16-accumulated-frame-l2

The registered replay passes normal and optimized primary checks, all 200 source-array symbols, 96 output rows, 104 route/frame lifts, 53,248 rank-one basis columns, 131,072 signed rank-eight kernel coefficients and ten semantic fault controls. A separate implementation checks 13,631,488 active characters and 594 scalar basis coordinates with noncommuting rational 2x2 algebra fixtures; five boundary tests cover corruption, source drift and read-only Git-free replay. Python 3.10.9 direct checks, package pins, selected binding-only baseline and whitespace checks also pass. This is author-checked; no separate-agent, independent human, formal-kernel or hosted-CI pass is claimed.

**Remaining obligations:** record capture/retention/retirement, output storage and consumption, physical map/address costs, child/output hosting, recursive precision/tape, all four bank repairs, full controller and all-size admission. The 224 bill has a changed output frame; 992 is the comparable old-frame bill. Counts are constructive upper invoices, not optimality or multiplication-runtime claims.

**Credit:** Ali Romman/PR1969 and the retained native/supplier lineage; Sagar Thakrar/PR2470 for L2; starship-s/PR2443 for the cut decoder; ywz65/PR2456/2468/2492 for the operator/native methods and precise cross-cut warning; Ross Richardson/PR2480 for the retention result. The directly compared PR2492 head is `9cc0d4d60819ddd246c9db9549f8ae4a61b68e45`. No pending predecessor verifier is imported or run; main's pinned scalar_cost function is evaluated in isolation.

The [package's next questions](https://github.com/WilliamLawyer/integer-mult-bounds/blob/e5500c43de15fdd09b5efb7629e46743e52273bd/research/qq16-accumulated-frame-l2/README.md) identify downstream consumption of the accumulated frame and a complete retained-record contract as follow-ups; these block using the smaller local invoice in a full supplier claim.

Prepared by **William Lawyer**, with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance in derivation, implementation, verification and writing. Apache-2.0. Targeted live overlap and source refreshes are recorded in VALIDATION; complete live Discussion pagination was unavailable, and an attempted advance claim returned 403, so no public reservation is asserted. This contribution is intended for independent review.
